model.rationale: André Carson holds a heavily Democratic Indianapolis seat with a large financial edge and no visible challenger campaign, and markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price his reelection near 97-98%. Nothing in the evidence suggests the D+21 baseline is out of place here.
model.watch: Any late personal scandal or outside-spending surge against Carson could narrow the margin, though history and the district's lean make that a low-probability path.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 7th District covers most of Indianapolis and carries a partisan lean of D+21, among the most Democratic territories in the state. André Carson has held the seat since a 2008 special election and is running again, backed by more than $1 million raised this cycle and roughly $620,000 in the bank. His Republican opponent, Patrick McAuley, shows no reported fundraising, and a Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No independent polls of the race and no expert ratings are available.

Prediction markets price Carson's reelection at roughly 97-98% on both Kalshi and Polymarket, and the structural fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and the money gap — all point the same way. The forecast expects Carson to win by a comfortable margin in the mid-20s, with the seat firmly in Democratic hands.
